reference.scenario: We are at the final part of a fictional interview. Ask questions that help you understand whether this role fits your goals. I will answer as the hiring manager of a small product team. Ask one question at a time and follow up on useful details.

facts.value: The first three months focus on shipping a small customer-facing improvement with a mentor.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about success or initial expectations

facts.value: The team documents major decisions asynchronously and has two shared meeting blocks per week.
A recent launch slipped because ownership between product and engineering was unclear. The team is trialing a single-owner decision log.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks for a challenge or concrete example

facts.value: A mentor meets weekly; urgent questions go to a rotating support partner.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about support or onboarding

model_points: Connects questions to the role, personal priorities and information still missing.
Uses the interviewer’s answer to deepen the next question.
Asks for examples instead of accepting broad culture claims.
Investigates expectations, support and tradeoffs relevant to a fit decision.
Uses limited time for important questions rather than exhausting a memorized list.
Summarizes what was learned and what remains uncertain without overclaiming.

probes.question: Is there a specific example you would like me to explain?
What did you learn that would matter to your decision?

follow_ups: What additional evidence would change your decision?
reference.exemplar_answer: Multiple approaches are valid. A strong response establishes the goal, uses the provided facts, tests alternatives, explains tradeoffs, and states uncertainty.

interviewer_notes: Roleplay only this fictional team. Do not invent compensation, legal policies, company names or personal history. Say when a fact is unspecified. Do not score candidates down for reasonable questions about working conditions or support.

learning_drills.title: Repair one decision
learning_drills.prompt: Choose one decision in your answer. Rewrite the explanation using one fact, one alternative, and one limitation. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: State what would change your mind
